shift.eyebrow: What the Case Study Taught Us
shift.title: Getting Found Is Only the First Step
story: For an established excavation and service business in Southern Ontario, we rebuilt the website, improved local SEO and Google Business Profile visibility, built dedicated pages for the services they wanted, and **added call and form tracking.**

The visibility work performed. Then the tracking showed something we hadn't been hired to look at: **more people were calling, not every call was answered, and form inquiries weren't consistently followed up.**
shift.pullQuote: We had successfully fixed a problem that was no longer the biggest one.
storyAfter: That's why ALL8 looks at the whole picture. Getting found is one of four stages, alongside getting contacted, responding and following up, and winning the work. Fixing only the first can leave the real problem untouched.

founder.title: Built on Real Trades Experience
paragraphs: ALL8 Webworks was founded by Matt McLennan, a licensed Ontario 310S Automotive Service Technician with a background in industrial contracting, construction operations, business development, and software engineering.

Matt spent 16 years with a multi-trade industrial contractor, working mainly in automotive diagnostics, fleet maintenance, and technical troubleshooting. That work gave him firsthand experience of what it takes to keep people, equipment, and projects moving.
He has also worked in excavation and construction operations, including fieldwork, estimating, bid preparation, project coordination, and business development.
Alongside that, Matt built his software skills by developing websites, applications, integrations, and automation designed to solve practical business problems.
Working across these areas showed him the same thing again and again: good businesses lose opportunities when their website, customer inquiries, and day-to-day processes don't work together.
ALL8 starts from how a contractor's business actually runs, where opportunities are being missed, and what will make a meaningful difference.
The goal is simple: help contractors get found, attract more qualified inquiries, follow up effectively, and win more work.

principles.title: Four Things We Don't Bend On

items.title: Diagnosis before proposal
items.body: We look at how customers find you, contact you and get followed up before recommending anything. If the highest-impact fix is something we don't sell, we'll say so.

items.title: Your accounts, your data
items.body: Your domain, content, ad accounts, analytics and customer records stay in your name. Scope and recurring fees are explained before work begins.

items.title: Measured, not asserted
items.body: Call and form tracking goes in early, so the work can be judged on leads and sources rather than impressions and adjectives. It also tells us when we've fixed the wrong thing.

items.title: Use what's already working
items.body: If your team already uses a CRM, quoting tool or scheduling software, we connect to it instead of replacing it. New tools get recommended when the current ones genuinely can't do the job.

who.title: Built for Contractors and the Trades
who.subtitle: Owner-operated and small-to-midsize contractors, where work comes in as calls, quote requests and estimates, and every missed one is expensive.
who.note: The trade matters less than how the work comes in. If customers find you on Google or by referral, call or request a quote, and then wait on someone to respond, the same four stages apply.
